column3: (2)  The  recording  of  such  statement,  shall  be  in
the person shall be informed of his rights under this
Act;
the  person  shall  have  access  to,  or  communicate
with, an Attorney-at-Law, if he so wishes;
the  person  shall  be  inquired  in  order  to  ascertain
whether such person wishes to voluntarily answer
the questions put to him, and the Magistrate shall
proceed to record a statement, only if he is satisfied
that  such  person  is  voluntarily  making  such
statement,  without  any  promise,  inducement  or
threat;
a questionnaire shall be obtained from the officer
in  charge  of  the  police  station  for  the  purpose  of
questioning  such  person;
the  person  shall  be  informed  that  he  has  no
obligation  to  answer  the  questions  being  put  to
him;
the  person  shall  be  warned  that  in  the  event  of
criminal proceedings being instituted against him,
the  contents  of  the  statement  that  he  will  make,
may be used as evidence against him;
whatever statement such person wishes to give shall
be  recorded,  in  addition  to  answers  given  to  the
questions put to him;
